h: Beverley: a cinema with a Minster on the doorstep
p: Flemingate puts this cinema in one of the best spots in town. Step outside and Beverley Minster is right there, one of the great Gothic churches of England, its twin towers looming over the rooftops. It's free to wander in, although donations are welcome, and it's well worth an hour before an evening film. Look out for the carvings and the ancient Frith Stool, a stone sanctuary seat that has been in the Minster for over a thousand years.

Beverley is a handsome, walkable market town. From the Minster, you can stroll up through the centre to the Saturday Market and on to North Bar, a medieval brick gateway that traffic still squeezes through today. St Mary's Church, near North Bar, is another stunner, with lots of detail to spot, including a carved rabbit that's said by some to have inspired the White Rabbit in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

On the edge of town, the Westwood is a huge area of common pasture where cattle still graze, criss-crossed with paths and lovely for a walk or a picnic. It's also home to Beverley Racecourse, which brings a crowd on race days, so check the calendar if you're driving in and parking matters.

The Treasure House, near the Minster end of town, combines a museum, art gallery and archives, and it's a good indoor option if the weather turns. With Hull only a short train or car ride away, Beverley makes a relaxed base for exploring the wider East Riding, from the Wolds to the coast.
Getting the most out of your visit

Parkway's mix of films, event cinema and live performances on the Hayward Theatre stage means there's often more than one reason to come back. Event screenings and live shows can be popular, so book those early. For families, a weekend matinee followed by a run around on the Westwood is a lovely way to spend an afternoon.

Because the railway station is within walking distance, it's an easy outing without the car. That's handy for anyone visiting from Hull or the coast who would like to enjoy a drink with tea before the film.
The café bar is a comfy place to wait if you arrive early, and the step-free access throughout makes it one of the easier venues in the area for wheelchair users and families with buggies.
